q: When no net external force acts upon it, a particle at rest will remain at rest and a particle in motion at a constant velocity will continue to move with the same constant velocity. This is _____ law.
e: When no net external force acts upon it, a particle at rest will remain at rest and a particle in motion at a constant velocity will continue to move with the same constant velocity. This is Newton's first law. Newton's first here means the inertia law: zero net force means constant velocity. Newton's second: net force equals mass times acceleration.

q: In mathematical form, if $F_{net}=0$ then a=_____ and v=constant(or)zero.
e: In mathematical form, if $F_{net}=0$ then a=0 and v=constant(or)zero. Net force and acceleration point the same way, and a equals F over m.

q: _____ is the natural property of a body which resists the change of its state of motion.
e: Inertia is the natural property of a body which resists the change of its state of motion. Inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion. Momentum: mass times velocity, so it is directed.

q: The inertia of a body is its reluctance to start moving, and its reluctance to _____ once it has begun moving.
e: The inertia of a body is its reluctance to start moving, and its reluctance to stop once it has begun moving. The physics in this sentence is built around stop.

q: Newton's first law is often referred as the law of _____.
e: Newton's first law is often referred as the law of inertia. Inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion. Force: a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion.

q: The net external force acting upon a particle is equal to the product of the mass and the acceleration of particle. This is _____ law.
e: The net external force acting upon a particle is equal to the product of the mass and the acceleration of particle. This is Newton's second law. Newton's second here means net force equals mass times acceleration. Newton's first: the inertia law: zero net force means constant velocity.

q: In mathematical form, Newton's second law is expressed as $F_{net}=$_____.
e: In mathematical form, Newton's second law is expressed as $F_{net}=$$ma$. Net force and acceleration point the same way, and a equals F over m.

q: The direction of the acceleration is the _____ as that of the net force.
e: The direction of the acceleration is the same as that of the net force. Same here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: As the magnitude of the force acting on a particle increases, the acceleration of the particle will increase accordingly. This means acceleration is _____ proportional to force.
e: As the magnitude of the force acting on a particle increases, the acceleration of the particle will increase accordingly. This means acceleration is directly proportional to force. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Newton's second law is also called law of force and _____.
e: Newton's second law is also called law of force and acceleration. Acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes. Mass: the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: Whenever two particles interact, the force exerted by the second on the first is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the force exerted by the first on the second. This is _____ law.
e: Whenever two particles interact, the force exerted by the second on the first is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the force exerted by the first on the second. This is Newton's third law. Newton's third here means action and reaction are equal, opposite, and on two bodies. Newton's first: the inertia law: zero net force means constant velocity.

q: In other words, for every action, there is an equal and _____ reaction.
e: In other words, for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. The physics in this sentence is built around opposite.

q: In mathematical form, Newton's third law is expressed as $F_{second on first}=$_____ $F_{first on second}$.
e: In mathematical form, Newton's third law is expressed as $F_{second on first}=$- $F_{first on second}$. Action and reaction are equal and opposite, and they act on two different bodies.

q: Action and reaction act as a pair at the same time but the pair of forces acts on _____ objects.
e: Action and reaction act as a pair at the same time but the pair of forces acts on two separate objects. Action and reaction are equal and opposite, and they act on two different bodies. The same: lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: Action force and reaction force _____ cancel out each other.
e: Action force and reaction force cannot cancel out each other. The physics in this sentence is built around cannot.

q: According to Newton's third law, it is not a single force acting by itself but a _____ of forces acting simultaneously.
e: According to Newton's third law, it is not a single force acting by itself but a pair of forces acting simultaneously. Action and reaction are equal and opposite, and they act on two different bodies.

q: In SI units, force that is acting on 1 kg mass to give it an acceleration of 1 m s⁻² is called 1 _____.
e: In SI units, force that is acting on 1 kg mass to give it an acceleration of 1 m s⁻² is called 1 newton. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: In SI units, 1 N = _____ kg m s⁻².
e: In SI units, 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻². SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: In CGS system, a force that is acting on 1 g mass to give it an acceleration of 1 cm s⁻² is called 1 _____.
e: In CGS system, a force that is acting on 1 g mass to give it an acceleration of 1 cm s⁻² is called 1 dyne. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: In CGS system, 1 dyne = _____ g cm s⁻².
e: In CGS system, 1 dyne = 1 g cm s⁻². The physics in this sentence is built around 1.

q: 1 N = _____ dynes.
e: 1 N = 10⁵ dynes. The physics in this sentence is built around 10⁵.

q: In FPS system, the unit of force is _____.
e: In FPS system, the unit of force is pound. The unit that belongs with this quantity is pound.

q: The slug is the unit of _____ in British engineering system.
e: The slug is the unit of mass in British engineering system. Mass here means the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location. Force: a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion.

q: When 1 pound force acts on a body and the acceleration of the body is 1 ft s⁻², the mass of the body is called 1 _____.
e: When 1 pound force acts on a body and the acceleration of the body is 1 ft s⁻², the mass of the body is called 1 slug. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: In FPS system, 1 lb = 1 slug ft s⁻_____.
e: In FPS system, 1 lb = 1 slug ft s⁻⁻². The physics in this sentence is built around ⁻².

q: Everybody attracts every other body in the universe. The gravitational force between the two bodies is directly proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. This is stated by _____ law of gravitation.
e: Everybody attracts every other body in the universe. The gravitational force between the two bodies is directly proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. This is stated by Newton's law of gravitation. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: In symbols, gravitational force $F \propto \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$ where r is the _____ between the masses.
e: In symbols, gravitational force $F \propto \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$ where r is the distance between the masses. Distance here means the path length travelled, with no direction.

q: According to Newton's law of gravitation, the gravitational force is _____ proportional to the product of the masses.
e: According to Newton's law of gravitation, the gravitational force is directly proportional to the product of the masses. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: According to Newton's law of gravitation, the gravitational force is _____ proportional to the square of the distance between the masses.
e: According to Newton's law of gravitation, the gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the masses. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: In vector notation, Newton's law of gravitation is expressed as $\vec{F}_{12} = -G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2} \hat{r}$ where G is called the gravitational _____.
e: In vector notation, Newton's law of gravitation is expressed as $\vec{F}_{12} = -G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2} \hat{r}$ where G is called the gravitational constant. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Force: a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion.

q: According to experimental measurements, the value of G in MKS system is found to be _____ m³kg⁻¹s⁻².
e: According to experimental measurements, the value of G in MKS system is found to be 6.67×10⁻¹¹ m³kg⁻¹s⁻². You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.

q: The value of G can also be expressed as _____ N m²kg⁻².
e: The value of G can also be expressed as 6.67×10⁻¹¹ N m²kg⁻². The physics in this sentence is built around 6.67×10⁻¹¹.

q: The attractions of the moon and the sun upon water of the earth cause _____.
e: The attractions of the moon and the sun upon water of the earth cause tides. The physics in this sentence is built around tides involving water.

q: Satellites are kept in their circular orbit by the gravitational attraction of the _____.
e: Satellites are kept in their circular orbit by the gravitational attraction of the earth. The physics in this sentence is built around earth.

q: A unit vector is a vector that has the magnitude _____.
e: A unit vector is a vector that has the magnitude 1. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: Four fundamental forces in nature are all field forces. They are the gravitational force, weak force, electromagnetic force and _____ force.
e: Four fundamental forces in nature are all field forces. They are the gravitational force, weak force, electromagnetic force and nuclear force. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: Among the four fundamental forces, _____ force is the strongest.
e: Among the four fundamental forces, nuclear force is the strongest. The physics in this sentence is built around nuclear.

q: Among the four fundamental forces, _____ force is the weakest.
e: Among the four fundamental forces, gravitational force is the weakest. The physics in this sentence is built around gravitational.

q: The _____ force is the second strongest force among the four fundamental forces.
e: The electromagnetic force is the second strongest force among the four fundamental forces. The physics in this sentence is built around electromagnetic.

q: Among the four fundamental forces, the gravitational and the electromagnetic forces are _____-range forces.
e: Among the four fundamental forces, the gravitational and the electromagnetic forces are long-range forces. The physics in this sentence is built around long.

q: Among the four fundamental forces, the weak force and nuclear force are _____-range forces.
e: Among the four fundamental forces, the weak force and nuclear force are short-range forces. The physics in this sentence is built around short.

q: The gravitational force acts between _____.
e: The gravitational force acts between objects. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: The electromagnetic force acts between electric _____.
e: The electromagnetic force acts between electric charges. The physics in this sentence is built around charges.

q: Weak force acts between _____ particles.
e: Weak force acts between subatomic particles. The physics in this sentence is built around subatomic.

q: Strong nuclear force acts between elementary particles such as proton, neutron, pion and _____ particles.
e: Strong nuclear force acts between elementary particles such as proton, neutron, pion and strange particles. The physics in this sentence is built around strange. Electron: the negative particle that orbits the nucleus.

q: When a spring is stretched or a plastic ruler is bent, the force that causes the spring and the ruler to retain their original form is called _____ force.
e: When a spring is stretched or a plastic ruler is bent, the force that causes the spring and the ruler to retain their original form is called elastic force. The physics in this sentence is built around elastic.

q: When a body is placed on a floor, the force between the two surfaces which resists the motion of the body is called _____ force.
e: When a body is placed on a floor, the force between the two surfaces which resists the motion of the body is called frictional force. Frictional names when a body is placed on a floor, the force between the two surfaces which resists the motion of the body.

q: The frictional force depends on the smoothness and cleanliness of the surfaces, the force pressing the two surfaces together and the _____ of the body.
e: The frictional force depends on the smoothness and cleanliness of the surfaces, the force pressing the two surfaces together and the speed of the body. Speed here means how fast the path length changes, with no direction. Mass: the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: Unlike gravitational force, frictional force and elastic force are _____ fundamental forces.
e: Unlike gravitational force, frictional force and elastic force are not fundamental forces. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: If a body is dropped from a height above the surface of the earth, it will fall onto the ground. This is due to the force of _____.
e: If a body is dropped from a height above the surface of the earth, it will fall onto the ground. This is due to the force of gravity. The physics in this sentence is built around gravity.

q: The weight of a body is the force of gravity acting on it which gives its acceleration when it is _____.
e: The weight of a body is the force of gravity acting on it which gives its acceleration when it is falling. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The acceleration due to the force of gravity is called acceleration due to gravity and it is represented by the symbol _____.
e: The acceleration due to the force of gravity is called acceleration due to gravity and it is represented by the symbol g. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: In MKS system, the value of g is approximately _____ m s⁻².
e: In MKS system, the value of g is approximately 9.8 m s⁻². The physics in this sentence is built around 9.8.

q: In MKS system, the value of g can also be expressed as 9.8 _____ kg⁻¹.
e: In MKS system, the value of g can also be expressed as 9.8 N kg⁻¹. The physics in this sentence is built around N.

q: In FPS system, g = _____ ft s⁻².
e: In FPS system, g = 32 ft s⁻². The physics in this sentence is built around 32.

q: The attracting force of the earth acting on a body is defined as the _____ of the body.
e: The attracting force of the earth acting on a body is defined as the weight of the body. Weight here means the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force. Mass: the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: If the mass of the body is m and a=g, the weight of the body is found to be w=_____.
e: If the mass of the body is m and a=g, the weight of the body is found to be w=mg. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: The relation w=mg is true not only for freely falling bodies but also for bodies on the _____.
e: The relation w=mg is true not only for freely falling bodies but also for bodies on the ground. The physics in this sentence is built around ground.

q: Weight is a _____ and is directed toward the center of the Earth.
e: Weight is a vector and is directed toward the center of the Earth. Vector here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. Scalar: a quantity that has magnitude only.

q: Since weight is force, units of weight are newton, dyne and _____, while the units of mass are kilogram, gram and slug.
e: Since weight is force, units of weight are newton, dyne and pound, while the units of mass are kilogram, gram and slug. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: _____ is the quantity of matter in a body.
e: Mass is the quantity of matter in a body. Mass here means the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location. Weight: the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force.

q: Mass is also a measure of _____.
e: Mass is also a measure of inertia. Inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion. Weight: the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force.

q: The mass of a body measures its _____.
e: The mass of a body measures its inertia. Inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion. Weight: the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force.

q: The mass of a body defined from the point of view of measuring inertia is called _____ mass.
e: The mass of a body defined from the point of view of measuring inertia is called inertial mass. Inertial names the mass of a body defined from the point of view of measuring inertia.

q: The mass defined by $m = \frac{W}{g}$ is called _____ mass.
e: The mass defined by $m = \frac{W}{g}$ is called gravitational mass. Gravitational names the mass defined by $m = \frac{W}{g}$.

q: Mass is a _____ and always a constant.
e: Mass is a scalar and always a constant. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. Vector: a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

q: Wherever a body may be, there is _____ change in the value of the mass of the body.
e: Wherever a body may be, there is no change in the value of the mass of the body. The physics in this sentence is built around no.

q: The weight of the body _____ change when its location is changed, but mass does not.
e: The weight of the body may change when its location is changed, but mass does not. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: Mass and weight are two _____ quantities.
e: Mass and weight are two different quantities. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass. Same: lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: According to Newton's law of gravitation, the gravitational force acting on a body at Earth's surface is $F = G \frac{mM}{R^2}$ where M is the mass of the _____ and R is the radius of the Earth.
e: According to Newton's law of gravitation, the gravitational force acting on a body at Earth's surface is $F = G \frac{mM}{R^2}$ where M is the mass of the earth and R is the radius of the Earth. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: The value of g near the earth's surface is calculated as g = G × M/R² = _____ m s⁻².
e: The value of g near the earth's surface is calculated as g = G × M/R² = 9.8 m s⁻². The physics in this sentence is built around 9.8.

q: Note that the value of g is independent of the _____ of the body.
e: Note that the value of g is independent of the properties of the body. The physics in this sentence is built around properties.

q: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a constant acceleration _____.
e: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a constant acceleration g. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: If the air resistance is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as _____ fall.
e: If the air resistance is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as free fall. By definition that quantity is free.

q: In free fall equations, we use the symbol h for displacement s and g for acceleration _____.
e: In free fall equations, we use the symbol h for displacement s and g for acceleration a. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The first equation of motion for free fall is v = v₀ + _____.
e: The first equation of motion for free fall is v = v₀ + gt. The physics in this sentence is built around gt.

q: The second equation of motion for free fall is v² = v₀² + _____, where h is the height.
e: The second equation of motion for free fall is v² = v₀² + 2gh, where h is the height. The physics in this sentence is built around 2gh.

q: The third equation of motion for free fall is h = v₀t + _____gt².
e: The third equation of motion for free fall is h = v₀t + 1/2gt². The physics in this sentence is built around 1/2.

q: The acceleration due to gravity g is directed _____ (towards the centre of the earth).
e: The acceleration due to gravity g is directed downwards (towards the centre of the earth). Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The value of g varies only slightly from one place to another, and therefore, its value is assumed to be _____ in the calculations.
e: The value of g varies only slightly from one place to another, and therefore, its value is assumed to be constant in the calculations. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Variable: a quantity that can change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: In solving free fall problems, displacement h will be positive if it is _____ the origin and negative below the origin.
e: In solving free fall problems, displacement h will be positive if it is above the origin and negative below the origin. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: In free fall problems, velocities v₀ and v will be positive if they are directed upward and negative if directed _____.
e: In free fall problems, velocities v₀ and v will be positive if they are directed upward and negative if directed downward. The physics in this sentence is built around downward.

q: Since acceleration g is always directed downwards, its value will be negative (i.e. g = _____ m s⁻²).
e: Since acceleration g is always directed downwards, its value will be negative (i.e. g = -9.8 m s⁻²). Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: According to Newton's second law, F = ma = m(v-v₀)/t, where another important physical quantity is the product of mass and _____.
e: According to Newton's second law, F = ma = m(v-v₀)/t, where another important physical quantity is the product of mass and velocity. Velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Acceleration: how quickly velocity changes.

q: Momentum (p) of a body is defined as the product of the mass of the body and its velocity, which is written as p=_____.
e: Momentum (p) of a body is defined as the product of the mass of the body and its velocity, which is written as p=mv. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Momentum of a body is directly proportional to its _____.
e: Momentum of a body is directly proportional to its velocity. Velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Mass: the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: Momentum is a _____ quantity.
e: Momentum is a vector quantity. Vector here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. Scalar: a quantity that has magnitude only.

q: Direction of momentum is the same as that of _____.
e: Direction of momentum is the same as that of velocity. Velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Acceleration: how quickly velocity changes.

q: Unit of momentum is expressed as the product of mass unit and velocity unit. In MKS system it is kg m s⁻_____.
e: Unit of momentum is expressed as the product of mass unit and velocity unit. In MKS system it is kg m s⁻⁻¹. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The law of conservation of momentum states that: If there is no net external force acting on an isolated system, the total momentum of the system is _____.
e: The law of conservation of momentum states that: If there is no net external force acting on an isolated system, the total momentum of the system is constant. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: The law of conservation of momentum is a general law and is true for both macroscopic and _____ objects.
e: The law of conservation of momentum is a general law and is true for both macroscopic and microscopic objects. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change involving true.

q: According to law of conservation of momentum, total momentum before collision = total momentum _____ collision.
e: According to law of conservation of momentum, total momentum before collision = total momentum after collision. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: In mathematical form, conservation of momentum for two bodies is: m_A v_A + m_B v_B = m_A v'_A + _____, where primed velocities are after collision.
e: In mathematical form, conservation of momentum for two bodies is: m_A v_A + m_B v_B = m_A v'_A + m_B v'_B, where primed velocities are after collision. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: In the conservation of momentum equation, v_A and v_B are velocities of the masses _____ collision.
e: In the conservation of momentum equation, v_A and v_B are velocities of the masses before collision. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: In the conservation of momentum equation, v'_A and v'_B are velocities of the masses _____ collision.
e: In the conservation of momentum equation, v'_A and v'_B are velocities of the masses after collision. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: When a compressed spring between two wooden balls is released, according to conservation of momentum, if total initial momentum is zero, the final total momentum will also be _____.
e: When a compressed spring between two wooden balls is released, according to conservation of momentum, if total initial momentum is zero, the final total momentum will also be zero. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: When two balls are pushed apart by a compressed spring, m_B v'_B = -m_A v'_A. The minus sign indicates that the two velocity vectors are parallel but _____ in direction.
e: When two balls are pushed apart by a compressed spring, m_B v'_B = -m_A v'_A. The minus sign indicates that the two velocity vectors are parallel but opposite in direction. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: By using the relation m_B v'_B = m_A v'_A (taking magnitudes only), inertial _____ can be measured.
e: By using the relation m_B v'_B = m_A v'_A (taking magnitudes only), inertial mass can be measured. Mass here means the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location. Force: a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion.
